warnings: River rafting resumes only in September‑October; book licensed operators (UTDB‑registered) early as slots fill quickly.
Taxi/auto fares can rise during peak yoga season (Oct‑Jan); always agree on price beforehand or pre‑book a ride.
Triveni Ghat steps are uneven; keep luggage light and watch your footing.
Bungee jump and higher‑grade rafting require good swimming ability and proper life‑jacket checks.

Unlicensed rafting operators on Mall Road undercut licensed operators at ₹200–400/person, routinely skip life‑jacket checks, overload rafts, and have no rescue protocol. Mitigation: Book only UTDB‑registered operators (counters display a Uttarakhand Tourism certification sticker) such as Aquaterra Adventures, Red Chilli Adventure, or Garhwal Himalayan Exploration, and inspect ISRS‑certified life jackets before boarding.

No metered autos – rates must be negotiated up‑front. Typical price ranges: Ram Jhula ↔ Laxman Jhula ₹60–80; within town ₹50–100. Risk of over‑charging during peak yoga season (Oct‑Jan). Mitigation: Agree on fare before boarding or use pre‑booked Ola/taxis.

Rafting age/grade restrictions: Shivpuri → Rishikesh (Grade 3‑4) costs ₹800–1,200/person with a minimum age of 14; Marine Drive (Grade 4‑5) costs ₹1,200–1,800/person and requires experienced swimmers. Mitigation: Choose grade matching your skill level and confirm age policy with the operator.
River rafting is suspended district‑wide from mid‑June to mid‑September (SDRF seasonal ban). October marks the restart; ensure bookings are made early as slots fill quickly.
Riverfront steps at Triveni Ghat are uneven; heavy luggage or bulky gear can be hazardous. Mitigation: Use a small backpack and keep belongings close to your body.
Taxi/auto fares may inflate during the peak yoga retreat season (Oct‑Jan); negotiate or pre‑book to avoid over‑paying.

All food in Rishikesh is legally vegetarian; restaurants serve dishes like Aloo Puri, Chhole Bhature, and Ashram Thali (₹80–150). No meat cross‑contamination risk, but egg availability varies (many places are ‘pure veg’).
Rafting camp kitchens serve only vegetarian fare (dal, rice, sabzi) and have no toddler‑specific options – carry your own snacks if you need specialised food.

Unsolicited ghat‑side puja touts demand ₹500–2,000 for unrequested ceremonies. Mitigation: Decline all such approaches and go directly to Parmarth Niketan’s reception for legitimate puja arrangements.
personalization_notes: Solo traveler seeking a mix of adventure and spirituality – itinerary balances high‑adrenaline river runs with quiet temple visits.
Moderate pace respects your preference for a relaxed flow, with ample rest periods between activities.
Budget‑friendly meals and accommodation keep overall costs low while still offering a premium dinner option for occasional splurge.
